mainTopic: The story of דוד המלך, the rising תהום, and the שם written on a shard; the depth of the earth; רבי ירמיה's question about the 'tenth step'; and the start of a ברייתא on the verse 'their faces toward the east.'
overview: The amud opens at the end of a story: the תהום rose while דוד dug the שיתין, and אחיתופל uses a קל וחומר from סוטה to permit writing the שם on a shard to stop the water. The water then sinks 16,000 אמות. דוד raises it back to 1,000 אמות with the fifteen שיר המעלות, and עולא learns that the earth's crust is 1,000 אמות thick. The גמרא then returns to the משנה. רבי ירמיה asks how 'the tenth step' is counted, and the question ends in תיקו. A ברייתא explains the extra words 'their backs toward the היכל' as an added act of disgrace. The גמרא also shows that the כהנים' declaration was worded so God's name is not said twice in a row. A new משנה sets the daily trumpet blasts in the מקדש at 21 to 48, reaching 48 on a ערב שבת during סוכות. The גמרא explains that רבי יהודה counts תקיעה-תרועה-תקיעה as one blast, giving 7 to 16. Each side brings a פסוק for its view. Finally, the גמרא ties רב כהנא's ruling to רבי יהודה and asks why that would need saying, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: דוד asks whether to throw the Name into the depths, and no one answers
steps.stepSummary: דוד finishes his question: may we write the שם on a clay shard and throw it into the תהום so the water stops rising? No one answers him.
steps.simpleTranslation: [May we write the Name] on a clay shard, throw it into the depths, and the waters will settle? There was no one who said anything to him.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a story. דוד asks the sages whether he may write God's Name on a shard to stop the flooding תהום, and the room goes silent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The halachic problem is that throwing the Name into water will erase it, and erasing the Name is normally אסור. The silence shows that nobody wanted to take responsibility for a ruling that permits erasing the Name.

keyTerms.meaning: The deep waters under the earth (תהום)
And it will settle down / rest
There is not / there was no one

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins mid-sentence. The words 'Is it permitted to write the Name' come on the previous amud, so 'on a shard' is the end of דוד's question.

phrases.english: on a clay shard, and throw it into the depths, and it will settle!
phrases.notes: The end of דוד's question about writing the Name.

phrases.english: There was no one who said anything to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun on the previous amud, in which דוד dug the שיתין and the תהום rose.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is it permitted to write the שם on a shard and throw it into the water, where it will be erased, in order to save the world?

steps.title: דוד curses anyone who knows the answer but stays silent
steps.stepSummary: דוד declares that anyone who knows what to say and does not say it should be strangled in his throat.
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד said: Anyone who knows what to say and does not say it, may he be choked in his throat.
steps.whatsHappening: דוד pressures the silent sages by cursing anyone who knows the answer and keeps quiet. This sets up אחיתופל's reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Staying silent here is not humility, because the world is in danger. דוד's curse forces someone who knows the answer to speak up.

phrases.english: David said:
Anyone who knows what to say and does not say it,
may he be choked in his throat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר דָּוִד: כׇּל דְּיָדַע לְמֵימַר וְאֵינוֹ אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the silence in Step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever knows the answer in a crisis must say it.

steps.title: אחיתופל's קל וחומר from the סוטה permits it
steps.stepSummary: אחיתופל argues with a קל וחומר: the Torah lets God's Name be erased in the סוטה waters to make peace between a husband and wife, so it is surely permitted in order to save the whole world. He rules: it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחיתופל made a קל וחומר on his own: If, to make peace between a man and his wife, the תורה said 'Let My Name, written in holiness, be erased on the water,' then to make peace for the entire world, all the more so! He said to him: It is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: אחיתופל finally answers דוד. He proves from the law of סוטה that erasing the Name is allowed here, and gives the ruling: 'שרי' (it is permitted).
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סוטה ritual, a scroll with God's Name is dissolved in water, so the Torah itself allows erasing the Name for שלום בית. אחיתופל reasons that if the Name may be erased for peace in one home, it may certainly be erased to save the whole world.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a smaller case to a bigger case (a fortiori)
Peace between a husband and wife
Will be erased in the water (the סוטה ritual)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source showing how highly the Torah values שלום: even God's holy Name may be erased for it.

phrases.english: Ahitophel made a kal vachomer on his own:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה לַעֲשׂוֹת שָׁלוֹם בֵּין אִישׁ לְאִשְׁתּוֹ,
phrases.english: If, to make peace between a man and his wife,
the Torah said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמִי שֶׁנִּכְתַּב בִּקְדוּשָּׁה יִמָּחֶה עַל הַמַּיִם,
phrases.english: 'My Name, which was written in holiness, shall be erased on the water,'
then to make peace for the entire world —
all the more so!
He said to him: It is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers דוד's question from Step 1 after the pressure in Step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is permitted, based on a קל וחומר from the erasing of the Name in the סוטה ritual.

steps.title: The Name is thrown in and the depths sink 16,000 cubits
steps.stepSummary: דוד writes the שם on a shard and throws it into the תהום. The waters drop 16,000 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He wrote the Name on a shard and threw it into the depths, and the depths went down sixteen thousand cubits.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. דוד acts on the ruling, and the waters drop far, 16,000 אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plan worked, but too well: the water did not just stop rising, it sank very deep. This sets up דוד's correction in the next step.

phrases.english: He wrote the Name on a shard
and threw it into the depths,
and the depths went down sixteen thousand cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the ruling from Step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The waters of the תהום sank 16,000 אמות.

steps.title: דוד raises the waters back up with the fifteen שיר המעלות
steps.stepSummary: Seeing that the water sank too far, דוד says the world is more fertile when the water is higher. He recites the fifteen שיר המעלות, raising the water 15,000 אמות so it rests 1,000 אמות below the surface.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he saw that it had gone down too much, he said: The higher it is, the moister the world. He said the fifteen Ascents, raised it fifteen thousand cubits, and set it at a thousand cubits.
steps.whatsHappening: דוד fixes the problem. The ground needs underground water nearby to stay moist and fertile, so he sings fifteen songs and brings the water back up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the fifteen שיר המעלות raised the water 1,000 אמות, for a total of 15,000. Since it had sunk 16,000, it now rests 1,000 אמות below the surface, a number עולא will use in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The fifteen שיר המעלות in תהלים
And he set it / established it

phrases.english: When he saw that it went down too much,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: כַּמָּה דְּמִידְּלֵי — טְפֵי מִירְטַב עָלְמָא.
phrases.english: he said: The higher it is, the moister the world.
He said the fifteen Songs of Ascents,
and raised it fifteen thousand cubits,
and set it at a thousand cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects the over-sinking described in Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The waters were set at 1,000 אמות below the surface.
steps.whatToRemember: 16,000 down, then 15,000 up, leaves the תהום 1,000 אמות below the earth.

steps.title: עולא: the earth's crust is a thousand cubits thick
steps.stepSummary: עולא learns from the story that the earth above the תהום is 1,000 אמות thick.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Learn from this that the thickness of the earth is a thousand cubits.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא draws a factual conclusion from the story's final number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the water was set 1,000 אמות down, the layer of ground on top of it must be 1,000 אמות thick. This claim is challenged in the next step.

phrases.english: Ulla said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ סוּמְכָא דְאַרְעָא אַלְפָּא גַּרְמִידֵי.
phrases.english: Learn from this that the thickness of the earth is a thousand cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the 1,000 אמות in Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The earth above the תהום is 1,000 אמות thick.

steps.title: Challenge: we dig a little and find water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that we see water come out after digging only a little, far less than 1,000 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we see that we dig a little and water comes out!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks עולא's claim using everyday experience.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תהום is 1,000 אמות deep, a shallow hole should never reach water. Yet shallow digging does reach water, which seems to contradict עולא.

phrases.english: But we see that we dig a little
and water comes out!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's statement in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that the earth is 1,000 אמות thick
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Observation shows water just below the surface, which contradicts a 1,000 אמה crust.

steps.title: רב משרשיא: that water comes from the rising פרת
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא answers that the shallow water comes from water rising up toward the פרת, not from the תהום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: That water is from the ascent of the פרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא defends עולא by explaining where the shallow water comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פרת flows at a high level, so water climbs up through channels underground to feed it, and that is what we hit when we dig. The real תהום is still 1,000 אמות down.

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya said:
That is from the ascent of the Euphrates.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא: הָהוּא מִסּוּלָּמָא דִפְרָת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the evidence: the shallow water comes from a different source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Shallow water shows that the תהום is close to the surface.
steps.terutzMaskana: Shallow water comes from the פרת's ascent. The תהום is still 1,000 אמות down.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: the priests at the Upper Gate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: two כהנים stood at the upper gate that leads down from עזרת ישראל to עזרת נשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the priests stood at the Upper Gate that descends' etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the story and returns to the משנה. It quotes the line about the כהנים with trumpets to set up a question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה continues that when the rooster crowed, the כהנים blew the trumpets, and blew again when they reached 'the tenth step.' That phrase is what רבי ירמיה will ask about next.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc. (the quote continues in the משנה)

phrases.english: And the priests stood at the Upper Gate
that descends, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה after the story about the תהום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהנים stood with trumpets at the upper gate on the fifteen steps.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה asks what 'the tenth step' means
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks whether 'the tenth step' means the tenth counting from the bottom (after going down five) or the tenth counting from the top (after going down ten, standing on the fifth).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: 'On the tenth step' — does it mean he went down five and stood on the tenth, or perhaps he went down ten and stood on the fifth?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks a precise question about how to count the fifteen steps in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are fifteen steps. Counting from the bottom, the tenth step is reached after going down five steps. Counting from the top, it is reached after going down ten steps, leaving the כהן on the fifth step from the bottom.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
'On the tenth step' —
does it mean he went down five and stood on the tenth,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא דְּנָחֵית עַשְׂרָה וְקָאֵי אַחַמְשָׁה?
phrases.english: or perhaps he went down ten and stood on the fifth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the משנה quoted in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is 'the tenth step' counted from the bottom or from the top?

steps.title: The question is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The question stays open: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends רבי ירמיה's question without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means no proof was found either way. The question remains open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand (the question is left unresolved)

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question from Step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We do not know whether 'the tenth step' is counted from the top or from the bottom.

steps.title: ברייתא: why must the verse add 'their backs toward the Sanctuary'?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks: since the פסוק says 'their faces toward the east,' don't I already know that 'their backs were toward the היכל ה׳'?
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: From the fact that it says 'and their faces toward the east,' don't I already know that 'their backs were toward the Sanctuary of God'?
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא begins examining the פסוק in יחזקאל quoted in the משנה. It asks why the verse adds words that seem obvious. This sets up the teaching that the next step gives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The היכל was on the west side, so anyone facing east already has his back to it. Since the phrase seems unnecessary, the ברייתא is preparing to learn something extra from it.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
From the fact that it says: 'and their faces toward the east,'

phrases.aramaic: אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁ״אֲחוֹרֵיהֶם אֶל הֵיכַל ה׳״?
phrases.english: don't I already know that 'their backs were toward the Sanctuary of God'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic based on the משנה's quote of the פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra teaching comes from the seemingly repeated phrase 'their backs toward the היכל ה׳'?

steps.title: The extra words show an added act of disrespect
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers its own question. The extra phrase 'their backs toward the היכל ה׳' teaches that the sinners also acted in a deliberately disgusting and disrespectful way toward the שכינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, why does the פסוק say 'their backs toward the היכל ה׳'? It teaches that they exposed themselves and relieved themselves facing 'downward' (a polite way of saying: toward God's Presence).
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question from Step 12. The extra words are not repetition. They add a new, worse sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Facing east already means your back is to the היכל, so the פסוק would not need to say it. Since it is said anyway, the ברייתא reads it as describing an extra act of contempt aimed at the היכל. The phrase 'כלפי מטה' is a respectful way to avoid writing 'toward Above' next to something disgusting.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the פסוק need to say this? (asking about extra words)
'Downward', a respectful substitute meaning toward the שכינה

steps.confusionAlert: 'כלפי מטה' does not literally mean downward here. It is a polite way of saying 'toward Above' (the שכינה), so that God is not mentioned directly next to such an ugly act.

phrases.english: Rather, why does the verse state:
'Their backs toward the Sanctuary of God'?
It teaches that they would expose themselves,
phrases.notes: An extra act beyond just turning around.

phrases.english: and relieve themselves 'downward.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's question about the seemingly extra words in the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק adds 'their backs toward the היכל'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words describe an added act of open contempt toward the שכינה.

steps.title: Quoting the declaration: 'We are to God, and to God are our eyes'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה: the declaration the כהנים made, contrasting themselves with the earlier sinners.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'We are to God, and to God are our eyes,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. This is a setup line: it is preparing to raise a problem with this wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the wording as quoted, God's name (יה) appears twice right next to each other: 'ליה וליה'. That detail is what the next step will challenge.

phrases.english: 'We are to God, and to God are our eyes,' etc.
phrases.notes: Notice that God's name appears twice in a row.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the פסוק about the sinners to the משנה's next phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהנים declared that they belong to God and look to God.

steps.title: Saying God's name twice in a row is a problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects using רבי זירא. Repeating a word of worship looks like addressing two powers, so how could the כהנים say 'ליה וליה'?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But רבי זירא said: anyone who says 'שמע, שמע' is like someone who says 'מודים, מודים' (and he is silenced).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording just quoted. Saying God's name twice in a row seems forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא teaches that repeating 'שמע' is as bad as repeating 'מודים'. Elsewhere we learn that someone who repeats 'מודים' is silenced, because it sounds like thanking two gods. 'ליה וליה' doubles God's name the same way, so it should be forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: Repeating 'We thank', which suggests two powers

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't Rabbi Zeira say:
Anyone who says 'Hear, hear'
is as if he said 'We thank, we thank'!
phrases.notes: That person is silenced, since it looks like worshipping two powers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording quoted in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'ליה וליה' in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Doubling a word of worship looks like addressing two powers (רבי זירא), and 'ליה וליה' doubles God's name.

steps.title: The real wording separated God's two mentions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the actual declaration was longer, so God's name never appeared twice in a row.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what they said: 'They bowed toward the east, but we are to God (we thank Him), and our eyes look in hope to God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by giving the full, correct wording. In it, words come between the two mentions of God.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's 'אנו ליה וליה עינינו' was a shortened quote. The real text puts 'אנחנו מודים' and 'ועינינו' between the two mentions of יה. This avoids the problem of sounding like two powers.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this is what they said

steps.whatToRemember: The ceremony ended with a turn toward the היכל and a declaration contrasting us with the sinners of the first מקדש. It was worded so that God's name is never doubled back-to-back.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what they said:
'They bow toward the east,'
'but we are to God (we give thanks),'
'and our eyes look in hope to God.'
phrases.notes: The two mentions of God are now separated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording (the משנה gave an abbreviated quote)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: They said God's name twice back-to-back.
steps.terutzMaskana: The full text puts other words between the two mentions of God's name.

steps.title: New משנה: the number of daily trumpet blasts in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sets a range of 21 to 48 trumpet blasts a day. It explains that the basic 21 are 3 for opening the gates, 9 for the morning תמיד, and 9 for the afternoon תמיד, plus 9 more on days with a מוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: They never sounded fewer than 21 blasts in the מקדש, and never more than 48. Every day there were 21 blasts: 3 for opening the gates, 9 for the morning תמיד, and 9 for the afternoon תמיד. On days with מוספין, they added 9 more.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins on a new topic: trumpet blasts in the מקדש. It gives the minimum and maximum, then explains the daily count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 3 + 9 + 9 = 21, the daily minimum. Days with a קרבן מוסף (like ראש חודש or יום טוב) get 9 extra blasts. The maximum of 48 will come from adding up all the possible extras on one busy day.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily communal offering, brought morning and afternoon

steps.confusionAlert: 'Fewer than 21 / more than 48' is a range for different days, not a choice. Every ordinary day has exactly 21, and special days add more.

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מֵעֶשְׂרִים וְאַחַת תְּקִיעוֹת בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ,
phrases.english: They sound no fewer than twenty-one blasts in the Temple,
and they do not add beyond forty-eight.
Every day there were there
twenty-one blasts in the Temple:
three for the opening of the gates,
nine for the morning daily offering,
and nine for the afternoon daily offering.
And with the additional offerings they would add nine more.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מֵעֶשְׂרִים וְאַחַת תְּקִיעוֹת בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The daily blasts range from 21 to 48. The base 21 are 3 + 9 + 9, and days with מוסף add 9.

steps.title: Six extra blasts on ערב שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: on ערב שבת six blasts are added. Three tell the people to stop working, and three mark the moment שבת begins.
steps.simpleTranslation: On ערב שבת they added six: three to stop the people from work, and three to separate between holy and ordinary time.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of extra blasts. Now it covers ערב שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first three blasts are a warning: finish your work, שבת is coming. The last three mark the exact start of שבת, the line between חול and קודש. This is another extra that will count toward the maximum of 48.

keyTerms.meaning: To separate holy time from ordinary time

steps.whyThisMatters: These ערב שבת blasts feed into the 48-blast maximum described in the next step.

phrases.english: And on Shabbat eve they would add six:
three to stop the people from work,
and three to separate between holy and ordinary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of added blasts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ערב שבת six blasts are added: 3 to stop work and 3 to mark the start of שבת.

steps.title: The maximum of 48 blasts on ערב שבת during סוכות
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists all 48 blasts blown on a ערב שבת that falls during סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: On a ערב שבת during the festival there were 48 blasts: 3 for opening the gates, 3 at the upper gate, 3 at the lower gate, 3 for filling the water, 3 on the altar, 9 for the morning תמיד, 9 for the afternoon תמיד, 9 for the מוספין, 3 to stop the people from working, and 3 to separate holy time from weekday time.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains how the maximum number, 48, is reached. It adds up every possible blast on the busiest day of the year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The day starts with the basic 21 blasts and adds 9 for the מוסף and 6 for ערב שבת, which makes 36. The extra 12 come from the water-drawing ceremony of סוכות (upper gate, lower gate, filling, altar). 36 + 12 = 48.

keyTerms.meaning: The upper gate of the עזרה, where blasts were sounded during the water-drawing ceremony
Filling the vessel with water for the water libation (ניסוך המים)
The additional offerings brought on שבת and יום טוב
To separate holy time from weekday time, marking when שבת begins

steps.whatToRemember: 48 is the maximum. It comes from ערב שבת falling during סוכות, when every kind of blast happens on the same day.

phrases.english: On a Shabbat eve that falls during the festival
there were forty-eight blasts there:
three for the opening of the gates,
three at the upper gate,
and three at the lower gate,
and three for filling the water,
phrases.notes: Part of the water-drawing ceremony of סוכות

phrases.english: and three on top of the altar,
nine for the morning daily offering,
and nine for the afternoon daily offering,
and nine for the additional offerings,

phrases.aramaic: שָׁלֹשׁ לְהַבְטִיל אֶת הָעָם מִן הַמְּלָאכָה,
phrases.english: three to stop the people from work,
and three to separate between holy and weekday.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת שֶׁבְּתוֹךְ הַחַג הָיוּ שָׁם אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמֹנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה's count by showing how the top of the range, 48, is reached
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ערב שבת during סוכות, 48 blasts are sounded.

steps.title: The משנה does not follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that our משנה disagrees with רבי יהודה, who gives a range of 7 to 16 blasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Our משנה is not like רבי יהודה. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says, one who blows the fewest may not blow fewer than seven, and one who blows the most may not blow more than sixteen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by pointing out that a ברייתא has רבי יהודה giving very different numbers from our משנה. This sets up the question of what the disagreement really is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said 21 to 48, while רבי יהודה says 7 to 16. Notice that each of רבי יהודה's numbers is exactly one third of the משנה's numbers. That is a hint that the argument is about counting, not about how many sounds were blown.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה does not follow the opinion of...
It was taught in a ברייתא
One who blows the fewest (the minimum)
One who blows the most (the maximum)

steps.whatToRemember: משנה: 21 to 48. רבי יהודה: 7 to 16. Each of his numbers is one third of the משנה's.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Our mishna is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.
As it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One who minimizes may not go below seven,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַמּוֹסִיף לֹא יוֹסִיף עַל שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה.
phrases.english: and one who adds may not add beyond sixteen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the numbers in the משנה with a ברייתא that has different numbers
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the range is 7 to 16 blasts.

steps.title: What is the disagreement about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what point רבי יהודה and the רבנן actually disagree on.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about what lies behind the different numbers. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether they argue about how many sounds were blown, or only about something else. The answer will show that the argument is only about how to count.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the numbers in the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the basic point the two sides disagree on?

steps.title: They disagree only about how to count
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה counts a set of תקיעה-תרועה-תקיעה as one blast. The רבנן count each sound separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה holds that תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה together are one. The רבנן hold that a תקיעה counts by itself and a תרועה counts by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that both sides agree on the actual sounds blown. They disagree only about whether a group of three sounds counts as one blast or as three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי יהודה, the set of three is one unit, so 21 sounds equal 7 units and 48 sounds equal 16 units. This is why his numbers are exactly one third of the משנה's numbers.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהודה wants fewer sounds blown in the מקדש. Both sides blow exactly the same sounds. The only question is how to count them.
steps.whatToRemember: The argument is about counting, not about practice: one unit of three (רבי יהודה) or three separate blasts (רבנן).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds:
tekia, terua, tekia is one blast,
and the Rabbis hold:
a tekia counts separately and a terua counts separately.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is whether תקיעה-תרועה-תקיעה counts as one unit or as three separate blasts.

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי יהודה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי יהודה learns that the three sounds count as one. This sets up a proof from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the disagreement is clear, the גמרא looks for each side's source in the תורה, starting with רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבי יהודה's view, which step 22 explained
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק shows that תקיעה and תרועה form one unit?

steps.title: The פסוק joins תקיעה and תרועה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוקים use the word for blowing a תקיעה when they describe a תרועה, which shows the two belong together as one unit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, 'And you shall sound a תרועה' (ותקעתם תרועה), and it is written, 'A תרועה they shall sound' (תרועה יתקעו). How can that be? It must be that תקיעה and תרועה together are one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings פסוקים that use a verb from the root of תקיעה to describe blowing a תרועה. It uses this to prove רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a תרועה is 'sounded' with a תקיעה-word, the תורה is joining the two sounds together. So the full set is one blast, not separate blasts.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall sound a תרועה' (במדבר י:ה)
How can this be? (introduces the resolution of two texts)

phrases.english: The verse states: “And you shall sound [utkatem] a terua”
and it is written: “A terua they shall sound [yitke’u]”
How can this be?
tekia and terua are one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23 with a source from the פסוק
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תורה describes a תרועה with a תקיעה-verb, so the two form a single unit.

steps.title: How the רבנן read the same פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן explain that the פסוק teaches something else: a תרועה must have a plain תקיעה before it and after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? That פסוק comes to teach that there is a plain blast before the תרועה and after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how the רבנן deal with רבי יהודה's פסוק. In their reading, it does not teach that the sounds count as one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן agree that a תרועה is always surrounded by תקיעות. They use the פסוק to teach that rule about the order of the sounds, not a rule about counting them.

keyTerms.meaning: A plain, straight blast, meaning a תקיעה

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?

phrases.aramaic: הַהוּא לִפְשׁוּטָה לְפָנֶיהָ וּלְאַחֲרֶיהָ הוּא דַּאֲתָא
phrases.english: That verse comes to teach a plain blast before it and after it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן: הַהוּא לִפְשׁוּטָה לְפָנֶיהָ וּלְאַחֲרֶיהָ הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unspoken challenge from רבי יהודה's פסוק against the רבנן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the פסוק for a different purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seems to prove that תקיעה and תרועה form one unit
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק only teaches that a תקיעה surrounds each תרועה

steps.title: Where does רבי יהודה learn the surrounding תקיעות?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יהודה used the פסוק for something else, the גמרא asks how he knows there is a תקיעה before and after the תרועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה, from where does he learn 'before it and after it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. רבי יהודה used up that פסוק for his counting rule, so he needs a different source for the order of the sounds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees there is a תקיעה before and after the תרועה. The question is which פסוק teaches that according to רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he learn it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda,
from where does he derive before it and after it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the רבנן's reading into a question about רבי יהודה's source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יהודה's source for the תקיעות before and after the תרועה

steps.title: He learns it from the word 'שנית'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns the surrounding תקיעות from the word 'שנית' (a second time) in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from the word 'a second time' (שנית).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה has a different word in the פסוק, 'שנית', which teaches the extra תקיעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'שנית' points to an extra plain blast. So רבי יהודה can use 'ותקעתם תרועה' for his counting rule and still have a source for the order of the sounds.

phrases.english: He derives it from “a second time.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'שנית' teaches the surrounding תקיעות.

steps.title: What is the רבנן's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks for the reason of the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what is their reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other side and asks for the רבנן's source. This sets up their proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we have only seen how the רבנן answer רבי יהודה's פסוק. Now we need their own positive source that each sound counts separately.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, what is their reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי יהודה's source to the רבנן's source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק shows that תקיעה and תרועה are separate?

steps.title: A תקיעה without a תרועה when gathering the people
steps.stepSummary: The תורה commands a תקיעה without a תרועה when gathering the people. That would make no sense if the two were one מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'When gathering the congregation, you shall sound a תקיעה and not a תרועה.' If you think תקיעה and תרועה are one, would the תורה say to do half a מצוה and not the other half?!
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן bring a פסוק where a תקיעה is blown alone. They use it to prove that a תקיעה counts by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the three sounds were one unit, a תקיעה alone would be only half of a מצוה. The תורה would not command half a מצוה, so each sound must be a full blast of its own.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind (introduces an idea in order to reject it)
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה or God

phrases.english: As it is written:
“And when gathering the congregation
you shall sound a tekia and not sound a terua.”
And if it enters your mind that
tekia and terua are one,
would the Merciful One say
perform half a מצוה
and do not perform the other half?!

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וּבְהַקְהִיל אֶת הַקָּהָל תִּתְקְעוּ וְלֹא תָרִיעוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28 with a proof from a פסוק
steps.raayaObject: The רבנן's view that a תקיעה counts by itself
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר י:ז, which commands a תקיעה without a תרועה for gathering the people

steps.title: רבי יהודה: that blast was only a signal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers that the lone תקיעה for gathering the people was only a signal, not a מצוה blast.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? That blast came merely as a signal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי יהודה deals with the רבנן's proof. The lone תקיעה was just a signal to gather the camp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because that תקיעה was not a מצוה blast at all, it is not 'half a מצוה.' So רבי יהודה can still say that a real מצוה blast is always the full unit of three. The next step gives the רבנן's reply.
steps.whatToRemember: Each side explains away the other's פסוק. רבי יהודה reads 'ותקעתם תרועה' as one unit and treats the gathering blast as only a signal. The רבנן read the lone gathering blast as proof that each sound counts by itself.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda?
That blast came merely as a signal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה: הָהוּא לְסִימָנָא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי יהודה against the proof in step 29
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the blast was not a מצוה blast
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A lone תקיעה would be half a מצוה, so the sounds must be separate
steps.terutzMaskana: The gathering blast was only a signal, so it says nothing about how מצוה blasts are counted

steps.title: The רבנן answer: a signal, but the תורה made it a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן agree the gathering תקיעה was a signal, but say the Torah made it a real מצוה. So their proof still stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say: It is a signal, but the Merciful One made it a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן push back against רבי יהודה's answer from the last step. They say a blast can be a signal and a מצוה at the same time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה tried to set aside the proof by calling the lone תקיעה 'just a signal.' The רבנן accept that it was a signal. They deny that this takes away its מצוה status, because the Torah itself commanded it. So a תקיעה with no תרועה can be its own מצוה, and that supports their view that the two are separate מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Rabbis (how do they respond?)
The Merciful One (a name for ה׳, meaning the Torah)
Made it, set it up as

steps.whatToRemember: Final positions: the רבנן say תקיעה and תרועה are separate מצוות, since the Torah commanded a lone תקיעה. רבי יהודה says they are one מצוה, and the lone gathering blast was only a signal.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis: It is a signal,
phrases.notes: The רבנן admit it served as a signal for gathering the people.

phrases.english: but the Merciful One made it a מצוה.
phrases.notes: Even so, the Torah commanded it, so it counts as a מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן: סִימָנָא הוּא, וְרַחֲמָנָא שַׁוְּיֵהּ מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's deflection in step 30 and restores the רבנן's proof from step 29.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי יהודה's claim that being a signal makes the lone תקיעה not a מצוה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Being a signal and being a מצוה are not exclusive. The Torah commanded the blast, so it is a מצוה even though it also works as a signal.

steps.title: Whose view does רב כהנא follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רב כהנא, who says there is no break at all between the תקיעה and the תרועה. It asks which side of the argument he follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this statement of רב כהנא follow: 'There is nothing at all between the תקיעה and the תרועה'? Whose view?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings in a new statement by רב כהנא and asks whose opinion it matches. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא rules that the תקיעה and the תרועה are blown with no pause between them, like one continuous sound. The גמרא wants to link this practical ruling to one side of the argument it just finished. The question 'כמאן' (like whom?) is said twice for emphasis.

keyTerms.meaning: רב כהנא, an אמורא who gives this ruling

steps.confusionAlert: רב כהנא is not saying the two blasts sound the same. He means there is no gap or pause between them; they are blown back-to-back as one connected sound.

phrases.english: Whose view does this follow,
that Rav Kahana said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בֵּין תְּקִיעָה לִתְרוּעָה וְלֹא כְּלוּם,
phrases.english: There is nothing at all between the tekiah and the teruah,
phrases.notes: No pause; they are blown as one continuous sound.

phrases.english: Whose view?
phrases.notes: The question is repeated for emphasis.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the finished argument between רבי יהודה and the רבנן to place a practical ruling of רב כהנא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which side of the argument, רבי יהודה or the רבנן, רב כהנא's no-pause ruling matches.

steps.title: It follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא's ruling matches רבי יהודה, who holds that תקיעה and תרועה are one מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: רב כהנא follows רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that the תקיעה and תרועה together make up one single מצוה. So it fits that they should be blown together with no break. According to the רבנן they are separate מצוות, so a pause would not be a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the view of רבי יהודה

phrases.english: Like Rabbi Yehudah.
phrases.notes: One מצוה means one connected sound.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב כהנא follows רבי יהודה, since treating תקיעה and תרועה as one מצוה explains why they are blown with no break.

steps.title: If it follows רבי יהודה, it's obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if רב כהנא just follows רבי יהודה, his statement seems obvious. Why say it at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is רבי יהודה, that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave. If רב כהנא simply follows רבי יהודה, he seems to add nothing new. This sets up an explanation that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה already said that תקיעה and תרועה are one מצוה. It seems to follow automatically that they are blown without a break. So the challenge is: what new point is רב כהנא teaching? The גמרא expects his statement to add something.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (a challenge that a statement adds nothing new)

phrases.english: (If it is Rabbi Yehudah,) that is obvious!
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 33 by arguing it makes רב כהנא's statement unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב כהנא's statement follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יהודה already holds תקיעה and תרועה are one מצוה, blowing them with no break follows automatically, so רב כהנא would be teaching nothing new.
